title: Siri alternatives for Mac in 2026: Lazur, Apple Dictation and Siri on price and privacy
metaTitle: Siri alternatives for Mac in 2026: price, privacy and what each does
description: Siri alternatives for Mac compared on price, privacy and features. See where Lazur, Apple Dictation and Siri each fit your daily work.
intro: The best Siri alternative for Mac depends on the job. Lazur is a voice assistant that sees your screen, points at things and answers out loud. Apple Dictation types what you say and has no length timeout. Siri is still Apple's own assistant, and its newest version, Siri AI, is in beta.
tldr: Lazur points at things on your screen and guides you one click at a time. It does not click for you.
Apple Dictation types your speech with no length timeout. It stops after 30 seconds of silence.
Apple has not published a Siri AI price. Check their pricing page before you decide.
Pick Lazur for help inside apps. Pick Apple Dictation for long typed text. Keep Siri for actions in Apple apps.

blocks.text: What a good Siri alternative for Mac needs to do

If you searched for a Siri alternative, you probably want one of three things. You want to type by voice faster. You want help inside an app you do not understand. Or you want a voice tool that answers out loud while you work.

Pick the job first, then pick the app. A dictation tool and a voice assistant are different products. Scoring them on one scale is unfair to both. The sections below compare each tool on the same jobs, using Apple's documentation and the facts we could verify, and they say where the other app wins.
Siri on Mac in 2026: what Apple says now

Apple now calls its assistant Siri AI. Its Siri page says Siri AI is in beta on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 and visionOS 27. Beta means features, limits and names can still change before release.

Apple describes a dedicated Siri app that syncs conversations across devices. It says Siri can take actions in apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It also says Siri can use personal context such as photos, emails and notes. Those are Apple's claims, so test them on your own Mac.

The price is the gap. Apple's Siri page does not state a price for Siri AI. It says expanded access to some features will be available for a fee in the future. It also says some features need an eligible iCloud+ plan, and that daily usage limits apply. Apple does not publish the amounts or the limits.

Apple's iCloud page lists iCloud+ 50GB at $0.99/month. That is storage pricing, not a Siri fee. Do not read it as the cost of Siri. Check Apple's Siri page again before you buy anything that depends on it.

blocks.title: Read the beta label
blocks.text: Siri AI is in beta. Apple may change the features, the limits and the fees before the final release. Write down the date you checked, and check again before you pay for anything.
Apple Dictation: the built-in Siri alternative for typing

Apple Dictation is the speech to text tool that ships with macOS. To turn it on, open System Settings, click Keyboard, then go to the Dictation section. Apple's Mac Help guide covers macOS 27, so older versions may show different settings.

Dictation runs for as long as you talk. Apple says you can dictate text of any length without a timeout. It stops on its own when no speech is detected for 30 seconds. If you pause longer than that, start it again.

Apple's improved on-device model fixes spelling, punctuation and capitalization. It is available in English on Macs with M3 or later and at least 12GB of unified memory. Dictation is not available in every language or region, and features may vary.
Say new line or new paragraph to add a break. If automatic punctuation gets in your way, turn it off in Keyboard settings. Dictation does not answer questions. It types what you say.

Reviews are mixed. A Tom's Guide headline on the iOS 27 beta calls the new dictation software new and improved. A review from Voibe, a company that sells its own dictation app, says Apple Dictation is accurate and responsive for everyday English. The same review says accuracy drops with specialized vocabulary. Read both as opinions, not tests.
Lazur: a Mac voice assistant that points and guides
Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘, Option and Command together, to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. It listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut.

Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.

Lazur also handles everyday voice work. That includes timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts. You ask in plain speech, and Lazur does the lookup or the step you asked for.

Background research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. That helps when you want several pages checked while you keep working.

Dictation is part of Lazur too, but it is not the headline. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots are included. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.
Worked example: getting unstuck in an app
Say you need a PDF from Pages, and you cannot find the export option. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. Lazur circles the control and labels it. Then ask Lazur to walk you through each step.

Lazur guides one click at a time. You click, Lazur waits, and then it points at the next control. You stay in charge of every click. That is slower than a shortcut you already know, but faster than hunting through every menu.

Apple Dictation cannot do this part. It types words. It does not point at controls or explain a menu. Apple's Siri page names actions in apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It does not describe pointing at controls, so test that before you rely on it.
Worked example: a long dictated email

Say you need to draft a long email in Mail. Turn on Dictation, then hold your shortcut and speak in full sentences. Say new paragraph where you want a break. Fix capital letters at the end, not in the middle of a thought.

Dictation keeps going while you keep talking. A pause of 30 seconds ends it. Plan your pauses. If you need to read back a line, do it with the keyboard, then restart the shortcut before the timer runs out. Lazur works in the same spot. Hold fn to dictate at the cursor, and use snippets for a closing line you send every day.
Where Siri and Apple Dictation beat Lazur
Lazur is not the best answer for every Mac user. Here is where the other two win.

items: Siri wins when your work lives in Apple apps. Apple says it can act in Messages, Music and Reminders.
Siri wins when you want Apple's cross-device sync. Apple says its Siri app syncs conversations across devices.
Apple Dictation wins when you want no extra app. It is built into macOS.
Apple Dictation wins when you dictate long text. Apple says there is no length timeout.
Lazur is not the right fit if you need Windows today. Windows is planned, not available.
Lazur is not the right fit if you want an app that operates your Mac for you. It guides you, and you do the clicking.

blocks.text: Price: what you can compare today
You cannot compare Siri and Apple Dictation on price from Apple's own pages. Neither page lists a price for them. Apple's Siri page says expanded access will cost a fee later, but it gives no amount.

Lazur's prices are on its pricing page. Pro is $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, with 150 AI actions. Power is $120/month, or $96/month annually, with 1,000 AI actions. A 3-day Pro trial starts when you first open the app, with no credit card.

Dictation is unlimited on both Lazur plans. So the plan limit applies to assistant requests, not to words you dictate. Count how many times a day you ask for help. Annual billing lowers Pro from $18 to $15 a month, and Power from $120 to $96 a month.
Privacy: what each Siri alternative says it does with your voice

Lazur says it listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored. Lazur says its content is never used to train AI models.

Apple says Apple Intelligence and Siri AI are designed to protect your privacy at every step. Its Private Cloud Compute commitments say your data is never stored and is used only for your requests. Apple calls its privacy promise verifiable. Read the full wording on Apple's Siri page.

Keyboard settings show whether general Dictation is processed on your device and not sent to Siri servers. Share Audio Recordings is a separate choice. If you turn it on, Apple can store audio of your Siri and Dictation interactions from your Mac. Choose Not Now to decline. You can change it under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

blocks.title: Check the audio setting
blocks.text: Look at Share Audio Recordings before you dictate sensitive text. Leave it off if you do not want Apple to store the audio of your Mac interactions.
Mistakes people make when they switch from Siri

items: Expecting Dictation to answer a question. It types words. It does not answer.
Expecting Lazur to operate your apps. It guides you one click at a time, and you do the clicking.
Pausing too long while you dictate. Thirty seconds of silence ends the session, so keep your pauses short.
Assuming Siri AI is free. Apple says expanded access will cost a fee later, and it gives no amount.
Dictating non-English text into the improved model. That model is English only.
Starting a trial and forgetting the date. The Lazur Pro trial runs for 3 days from your first launch.

blocks.text: How to test two Siri alternatives in one afternoon

items: Turn on Dictation. Open System Settings, click Keyboard, then go to the Dictation section.
Dictate a real email or note. Count the words you have to fix by hand.
Start the Lazur trial. It begins when you first open the app. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where a button in an app you use is.
Ask Lazur to walk you through one task you do every week. Note each click it asks you to make.
Write down which tool you reached for without thinking. That is the one that fits your work.

faq.question: Is there a free Siri alternative for Mac?
faq.answer: Apple Dictation is built into macOS, and Apple's Mac Help guide lists no price for it. Check their pricing page to confirm before you rely on that. Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. After the trial, Pro starts at $15/month billed annually.

faq.question: How much does Siri cost on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple has not published a Siri AI price. Its Siri page says expanded access to some features will be available for a fee in the future. It also says some features need an eligible iCloud+ plan. Apple's iCloud page lists iCloud+ 50GB at $0.99/month, which is storage pricing, not a Siri fee.

faq.question: Can Apple Dictation type a long document?
faq.answer: Yes. Apple says you can dictate text of any length without a timeout. It stops on its own when no speech is detected for 30 seconds. Start it again with your shortcut and keep going.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Ask Lazur where something is, and it circles the control and adds a label. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Which Macs get the improved Dictation model?
faq.answer: Apple says the improved on-device model needs a Mac with M3 or later and at least 12GB of unified memory. It works in English only. Open System Settings, click Keyboard and check the Dictation section to see what your Mac supports.

verdict: Pick Lazur if you want a voice assistant that sees your screen, points at controls and guides you one click at a time. Pick Apple Dictation if your main job is typing long text by voice in the Mac apps you already use. Stay with Siri if you want actions in Messages, Music and Reminders, and you can accept that Apple has not published Siri AI pricing yet.
